name: Anna
overview: Anna was a female prophetess from the tribe of Asher, recognized in Scripture for her role as a prophetess. She is uniquely identified by this title, which highlights her spiritual role in the biblical narrative. No additional personal notes are provided beyond her tribal affiliation and gender.
namesAndTitles: The name Anna means 'favor,' as recorded in Luke 2:36. This proper name does not appear to be given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew name common in the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Anna was the daughter of Phanuel. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Anna's significance in Scripture centers on her identity as a prophetess from the tribe of Asher, marking her as a recognized spiritual figure. Her mention in Luke 2:36 highlights her role in the unfolding of God's redemptive plan during the early life of Jesus. This brief but distinct identification underscores her importance as a faithful witness within the biblical narrative.
